# 2 Samuel 9 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** 2 Samuel 9 (13 verses)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA
**Total disagreements logged:** 9

---

## V.1 — "covenant-faithfulness" vs. "faithful love"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "covenant-faithfulness" / **PNEUMA:** "faithful love"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "covenant-faithfulness" — per project convention; "faithful love" loses covenantal dimension.

---

## V.2 — "summoned" vs. "called" vs. "brought before"
- **EMET:** "called" / **LOGOS:** "summoned" / **PNEUMA:** "brought before"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "summoned" — fits royal court context; PNEUMA adds action not in text.

---

## V.3 — "stricken of feet" vs. "crippled in his feet" vs. "crippled in both feet"
- **EMET:** "stricken of-feet" / **LOGOS:** "crippled in his feet" / **PNEUMA:** "crippled in both feet"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "crippled in his feet" — PNEUMA's "both" anticipates v.13; EMET too archaic.

---

## V.7 — "field" vs. "land"
- **EMET:** "field" / **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** "land"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "land" — *sadeh* as landed estate; "land" appropriate for royal holdings.

---

## V.7 — "grandfather" vs. "father"
- **EMET:** "father" (literal) / **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** "grandfather"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "grandfather" — *avikha* = "your father" but refers to Saul (Mephibosheth's grandfather).

---

## V.8 — "turned to" vs. "show regard to" vs. "notice"
- **EMET:** "turned to" / **LOGOS:** "show regard to" / **PNEUMA:** "notice"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "regard" — *panah* = turn toward/regard; PNEUMA too casual for court speech.

---

## V.10 — "bread" vs. "food"
- **EMET:** "bread" (*lechem*) / **LOGOS:** "bread" / **PNEUMA:** "food"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "food to eat" — *lechem* can mean food generally; farmland produce is broader than bread.

---

## V.11 — Speaker ambiguity
- **EMET:** preserves MT awkwardness / **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** smooth into narration
- **SOPHIA ruling:** narration — "So Mephibosheth ate at David's table." The MT is textually ambiguous.

---

## V.12 — "dwelling" vs. "who dwelt" vs. "living"
- **EMET:** "the dwelling of the house of Ziba" / **LOGOS:** "who dwelt" / **PNEUMA:** "living in"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "all who dwelt in Ziba's house" — LOGOS best captures the Hebrew construction.

---
*— SOPHIA*
